mintAuthority.summary: REUSD's immutable token accepts its Core owner or authorized operators for minting without collateral checks or a durable supply ceiling. Core's Voter currently uses a seven-day voting period followed by a one-day execution delay, but Core can directly mint or authorize arbitrary operators through its execution path. Exhaustive operator, hook, guardian and registered-pair closure is not certified, so D14 is unbounded and D29 is withheld; reconciliation is not-applicable.

mintIncidents.summary: Resupply's crvUSD/wstUSR market exploit manipulated exchange-rate and solvency logic so negligible collateral could borrow up to the reUSD debt limit, leaving bad debt through the stablecoin borrow route.

controls.label: REUSD owner — Resupply Core governance contract
controls.evidence: At Ethereum block 26095801, REUSD owner() returned Core 0xc07e000044f95655c11fda4cd37f70a94d7e0a7d and Core.voter() returned 0x11111111063874ce8dc6232cb5c1c849359476e6. Voter executionDelay() was 86400 and votingPeriod() was 604800 seconds. Verified Stablecoin source allows owner or operators to mint and lets only Core set token operators. Registry is an active token operator, correcting the previous no-direct-operator statement. Core's previously reviewed per-selector emergency permissions are not exhaustively re-audited by these reads.

controls.label: Resupply Registry: registered-pair mint operator
controls.evidence: At Ethereum block 26095801, REUSD operators(Registry) returned true. Registry mint(receiver,amount) requires pairsByName[IERC20Metadata(msg.sender).name()] == msg.sender, then invokes token.mint(receiver,amount). The current pair registry returns 22 addresses. This is native issuance through registered collateral pairs, not a bridge controller.

review.evidence: Historical governance review at Ethereum block 25321527 identified Core ownership, the token-weighted Voter with 30% quorum, seven-day voting and one-day execution delay, and emergency multisig permissions; the 2026-10-01 review corrected the earlier no-direct-operator claim by proving Registry is an active token operator for registered lending pairs. D14/D29 sweep 2026-10-03 at Ethereum block 26113561 (hash 0xf8669491a2d5c3e0dfe4c4233ed6861dcbe45f046fac9804a60c40ae5ee6846e): verified Stablecoin.mint allows Core owner or operators to mint any amount to any recipient without checking posted collateral or a durable bound; only Core can set token operators. A one-REUSD eth_call from Core to 0x000000000000000000000000000000000000beef succeeded without collateral calldata; no transaction was submitted. Core.execute admits arbitrary Voter calls and selector-permitted operator calls, so the old inference that collateralized current pairs or a governance delay makes root mint capacity raiseable is superseded: D14 is unbounded. Core.voter(), votingPeriod(), executionDelay() and quorumPct() remain 0x11111111063874ce8dc6232cb5c1c849359476e6, 604800, 86400 and 3000 respectively. There is no separate Core TimelockController: Voter._canExecute itself enforces createdAt + votingPeriod + executionDelay. Source permits Core to alter those parameters, replace Voter and authorize selector-level operators. OperatorSet history replay resolved 23 active permission tuples, including global selector and upgrade grants. GovStaker epoch weights are sourced, but admission to the allowed voting-power modes and every runtime/signer-bound execution path are not certified. D29 is withheld because global operator selector reach, hook behavior, guardian upgrades, parameter-reduction paths and all registered-pair/direct-operator mint paths lack complete closure certificates. Current seven-plus-one-day timing is not falsely promoted to a minimum unavoidable delay across all roots. No governedIssuance or unbounded-governed posture is authored; not-applicable reconciliation and no supervision yield unbounded-unreconciled.
